steps.title: Confirm the basic facts on the official DPWH page
sub: Budget, location, status, dates and bidders match this page.

steps.title: Open the bid documents
sub: Look for the quantities, a Bill of Quantities and technical specifications.

steps.title: Read Claude's check and confirm its points against the sources
Verify the risk: Contractor history and performance
sub: Open the blacklist entry and compare the licence (PCAB) number, address and company type with the bidder's.
Check that the debarment period covers the bid date; debarments expire.
Check whether the matched firm won or lost; a losing bidder matters less once the contract is awarded.
Open the winner's reported projects on the DPWH Transparency Portal and read what citizens reported.
Plan a site visit or ask a local monitor (Bisto Proyekto, TAPAT) to look once work starts.

steps.title: Verify the risk: Contractor ownership, affiliation and bidding networks
sub: Read the source article; confirm the link is stated there, not inferred.
Look for an official document (SEC filing, COA report, Ombudsman complaint) that confirms it.

steps.title: Verify the risk: Political economy and power concentration
sub: Read the source for any company–official link. Political-family context is background only: a family name is never evidence.

If an AMO name matches an official: confirm it is the same person (middle name, age, address, SEC filings) before relying on it. Search the surname on Pulitiklan (pulitiklan.com) and PCIJ's political dynasties database (pcij.org/political-dynasties).
Check the AMO and owners in the firm's SEC filings; the PCAB list names only the AMO.

steps.title: Check site and field evidence
sub: Check the site before work starts: satellite imagery of the stretch, earlier contracts on the same road, and whether a local monitor (Bisto Proyekto, a TPM civil-society partner) can take geotagged photos later.

steps.title: Check the rule behind any threshold you are relying on
sub: Every threshold BantAI uses comes from a published rule. See Policies & Manuals for the procurement law, the slippage and termination circulars, the CPES guidelines and the field-monitoring manual.

steps.title: Write down what you found and keep the documents you relied on
sub: Screenshots, Bill of Quantities pages, photos or letters: attach them with your decision.

memo.subject: Request for review: DPWH road contract 26GE0037, Guimaras, ₱21.1 million
memo.rank: BantAI places it ranked 39 of 51 Red cases in Region VI on the current list
background: Fragmented procurement records and limited oversight capacity make it difficult to identify which Philippine road projects need closer scrutiny. The Commission on Audit's 2024 Annual Audit Report on the DPWH reported locally funded projects worth ₱138.23 billion that were not efficiently implemented: 1,435 finished late (₱77.4 billion), 523 suspended (₱33.6 billion), 491 carrying negative slippage of 10 per cent or more (₱19.2 billion), 114 not started (₱6.72 billion) and 33 terminated (₱1.29 billion) — 2,596 projects in all, most of them identified only after the money had been spent.

Project BantAI addresses this gap through AI-assisted risk screening that supports timely, targeted human review. It integrates public DPWH and PhilGEPS data and checks each contract against risk indicators that were tested on past project outcomes. A reviewer verifies the evidence before any case is referred, so that oversight offices can make informed decisions on which contracts to examine first.
memo.disclaimer: This is a request for review, not a finding of irregularity. BantAI ranks contracts by tested risk signs so that limited audit time can go to the contracts most worth a look. A sign is a reason to check, not evidence of wrongdoing, and several ordinary explanations may fit any of them.
